title: Athletic Stance and Ready Position
objective: Develop a balanced athletic stance that allows players to accelerate, decelerate or change direction efficiently in response to a football movement cue.
groundSize: One 4 × 4-metre movement square for every four players.
equipment: Coloured markers or coach signal cards
coachingDifficulty: 1 – Simple organisation; minimal observation or intervention required.
setup:
Create several 4 × 4-metre squares.
Position one player in the centre of each square.
Other players wait outside the square and rotate after each work period.
Players begin without a football before progressing to holding a football.
The coach stands where all players can see or hear the movement cues.
howTheDrillWorks:
Each player adopts an athletic ready position with feet slightly wider than hip width, knees flexed and bodyweight balanced through the middle of both feet.
The coach checks posture before calling a direction: forward, backward, left or right.
Players take two quick adjustment steps in the nominated direction and immediately reset into the ready position.
The coach varies the timing and order of the cues.
After four to six cues, players relax and another player enters the square.
Once technique is stable, players repeat while carrying a football in two hands.
Complete three to five short rounds per player.
coachingPoints: Keep the head upright and eyes forward rather than looking at the ground.
Maintain soft knees and hips so movement can begin immediately.
Keep the chest over the knees without bending excessively at the waist.
Distribute bodyweight evenly rather than leaning heavily onto the heels.
Use short adjustment steps when resetting.
Keep the feet active and avoid locking the legs.
When holding a football, keep it secure but away from the chest enough to permit natural arm movement.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players can move in every direction without first shifting their bodyweight excessively.
Whether the knees remain aligned over the feet.
Whether the head and chest remain controlled during movement.
Whether players return to a balanced position after each cue.
Whether football security affects posture or movement quality.

commonErrors.error: Player stands upright with locked knees.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips slightly and maintain soft knees.

commonErrors.error: Weight sits heavily on the heels.
commonErrors.correction: Shift the chest marginally forward and feel pressure through the middle of the feet.

commonErrors.error: Feet are positioned too close together.
commonErrors.correction: Widen the base until the player can resist a light shoulder-level push without stepping.

commonErrors.error: Player looks down while moving.
commonErrors.correction: Place a visual target in front of the player and require eyes to remain on it.

commonErrors.error: Player crosses the feet during short lateral movements.
commonErrors.correction: Use quick push-and-recover steps while keeping the feet underneath the body.

progressions: Introduce visual colour cues instead of spoken directions.
Require a three-step acceleration before resetting.
Add a football and include a handball or kick after the final cue.
Pair players so one leads and the other mirrors.
Reduce the time between cues.
regressions: Use only forward and backward movement.
Allow players to walk through each direction before increasing speed.
Mark exact foot positions with flat markers.
Provide a demonstration before every repetition.
successIndicators: Begin in a balanced, repeatable athletic stance.
Move in any direction without a large preparatory step.
Keep their eyes forward while responding.
Reset under control after each movement.
Maintain football security without becoming rigid.
matchApplication: Australian football players frequently need to react from a stationary or low-speed position before leading, defending, collecting a loose football or responding to a turnover. A balanced ready position reduces reaction time and allows the player to move effectively in any direction.
relatedDrills: EA-002 – Single-Leg Balance and Body Control

title: Backpedal-to-Sprint Transition
objective: Develop the ability to move backwards under control, recognise a forward cue and transition rapidly into an effective acceleration line.
groundSize: Movement lanes approximately 15 metres long and 5 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours.
setup:
Mark a starting line, a five-metre backpedal zone and two diagonal acceleration gates.
Position one player at the starting line facing the coach.
Place a football feeder beyond each acceleration gate.
Other players wait outside the movement lane.
Ensure the backpedal area is level and clear.
howTheDrillWorks:
The player begins in an athletic stance facing the coach.
On the first signal, the player backpedals through the marked zone using short, controlled steps.
The coach displays a left or right directional cue.
The player plants, opens the hips and turns towards the nominated gate.
The player accelerates forward through the gate.
The feeder handballs the football into the player’s running path.
The player receives, returns the handball and exits the lane.
Players rotate after every repetition.
Complete three to five turns through each gate.
coachingPoints: Keep the hips low and chest controlled while backpedalling.
Use short steps rather than reaching backwards.
Keep the feet underneath the body.
Avoid allowing the heels to become the main contact point.
Open the hips before beginning forward acceleration.
Turn through the shortest efficient path.
Locate the football immediately after turning.
Accelerate through the gate rather than slowing to receive.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player remains balanced while moving backwards.
Whether the feet cross during the backpedal.
Whether the hips open efficiently after the cue.
Whether acceleration begins immediately after turning.
Whether the football is received without a major reduction in speed.

commonErrors.error: Player takes long backward steps.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the contacts and keep the feet beneath the hips.

commonErrors.error: Player stands upright while backpedalling.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain soft knees and a stable athletic posture.

commonErrors.error: Feet cross before the turn.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the base open and use a clear plant before rotating.

commonErrors.error: Player spins without gaining ground.
commonErrors.correction: Open the hips towards the gate and drive forward immediately.

commonErrors.error: Player loses sight of the feeder.
commonErrors.correction: Turn the head as the hips begin to open.

progressions: Add a second directional cue during the acceleration.
Begin with lateral movement before backpedalling.
Add a chasing player.
Require a kick after receiving.
Use a bouncing football rather than a handball feed.
successIndicators: React correctly to the directional cue.
matchApplication: Players frequently move backwards while defending space, tracking a forward or reading a high football before needing to turn and sprint towards an opponent, loose football or support position.

title: Mark, Play On and Escape Pressure
Pressure Receive and One-Step Release
primarySkill: Rapid disposal after receiving under pressure
objective: Develop the ability to receive possession, organise the body within one step and release accurately before defensive pressure arrives.
groundSize: Triangular grids approximately 12 metres on each side.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction.
setup:
Position a feeder at the first point of a triangle.
Place the receiver at the central point.
Position two target players at the remaining points.
Place one defender two metres behind the receiver.
Assign each target a different colour.
The defender uses two-hand touch pressure.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver begins scanning both targets.
The feeder handballs to the receiver.
As the football travels, the coach or feeder calls a target colour.
The defender begins closing from behind.
The receiver catches, takes no more than one organising step and disposes to the nominated target.
The receiver may pivot or release from the receiving side depending on the target.
The defender attempts a two-hand touch after the catch.
Players rotate clockwise after each repetition.
Repeat with the defender starting from different angles.
coachingPoints: Scan both targets before the football arrives.
Present the hands early.
Receive in front of the body.
Keep the feet active.
Use one efficient organising step.
Turn the hips towards the target.
Protect the football during the transfer.
Release before pressure reaches the body.
Maintain disposal accuracy rather than rushing blindly.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the receiver scans before possession.
Whether the football is caught cleanly.
Whether footwork efficiently aligns the body.
Whether the correct target is selected.
Whether release occurs before contact.
Whether handball accuracy remains high.

commonErrors.error: Receiver waits to scan until after catching.
commonErrors.correction: Identify both options before the feed.

commonErrors.error: Player catches against the chest.
commonErrors.correction: Present the hands and cushion in front.

commonErrors.error: Receiver takes several unnecessary steps.
commonErrors.correction: Use one organising step and release.

commonErrors.error: Player turns only the shoulders.
commonErrors.correction: Align the hips and feet towards the target.

commonErrors.error: Disposal becomes inaccurate under pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed and preserve handball technique.

progressions: Allow the target players to move.
Use a kick instead of a handball release.
Add a second defender closing another target.
Permit the receiver to choose the best option rather than follow a colour call.
Continue into a give-and-go sequence.
successIndicators: Organise the body within one step.
matchApplication: Players receiving around stoppages or congestion often have almost no time to hold the football. Early scanning and efficient footwork allow possession to continue before the tackler arrives.

title: Pressure, Contest and Evasion Phase Assessment
objective: Assess whether players can collect, protect and move the football effectively while responding to contact, multiple defenders, restricted space and support options.
groundSize: An area approximately 50 × 35 metres divided into six connected assessment zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback.
setup:
Create six connected assessment zones:
Ground-Ball Collection Zone: A player gathers under closing pressure.
Dual-Side Pressure Zone: Pressure may arrive from either side.
Contact Escape Zone: The player absorbs controlled contact and remains balanced.
Multiple-Defender Zone: The player chooses between splitting or escaping around two defenders.
Support Decision Zone: The player decides between evasion and release to teammates.
Transition Finish Zone: The attacking group exits pressure and completes a forward disposal.
Assign attackers, defenders, support players and targets to each zone.
Use Developing, Competent and Advanced ratings.
Set contact intensity appropriate to the group.
Complete one familiarisation run before assessed repetitions.
Position coaches to observe specific movement and decision behaviours.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first player approaches a rolling or bouncing football in the collection zone.
The player scans, gathers in two hands and moves away from the first defender.
The player enters the dual-side pressure zone where one defender closes from an unpredictable side.
The player transfers the football and protects possession.
In the contact zone, the player absorbs controlled side pressure and remains on the feet.
The player enters the multiple-defender zone and chooses whether to attack the split or move outside.
Two support players then present in separate lanes.
The ball carrier decides whether to continue carrying or release to support.
The attacking group exits through an open gate.
All attackers transition into the final zone.
The possession finishes with an accurate disposal to a moving target.
If defenders win possession, they counterattack towards the starting gate.
Each player completes at least two assessed repetitions in different roles.
Coaches record technical execution, decision quality, safety and match transfer.
coachingPoints: Scan before every major possession or movement action.
Secure the football before attempting to evade.
Use the first step to move away from pressure.
Carry in two hands until the pressure side is clear.
Transfer the football early and protect legally.
Maintain active feet through contact.
Avoid blind spins or repeated direction changes.
Assess both defenders before selecting the escape line.
Use support when it offers the safer or faster exit.
Accelerate after creating separation.
Preserve disposal quality under fatigue and pressure.
Transition immediately after the football leaves congestion.
React without delay when possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Scanning before collection and reception.
Clean two-hand possession.
First-step movement away from pressure.
Football transfer and protection.
Balance through controlled contact.
Safe hip, knee and ankle alignment.
Recognition of multiple defenders.
Selection of evasion or support.
Acceleration after separation.
Disposal accuracy under pressure.
Transition speed.
Immediate response to turnovers.
Decision quality across repeated efforts.

commonErrors.error: Player lowers the head without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Check pressure before entering the collection zone.

commonErrors.error: Attacker moves before securing the football.
commonErrors.correction: Gather firmly in two hands before escaping.

commonErrors.error: Football remains on the pressure side.
commonErrors.correction: Transfer early to the protected side.

commonErrors.error: Player stops the feet through contact.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain short driving steps and a low base.

commonErrors.error: Attacker uses a blind spin.
commonErrors.correction: Keep vision connected to the exit and use a compact turn.

commonErrors.error: Player attacks a closing split between defenders.
commonErrors.correction: Recognise when the gap has disappeared and move outside.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier ignores available support.
commonErrors.correction: Engage one defender and release to the spare teammate.

commonErrors.error: Disposal quality collapses after escape.
commonErrors.correction: Regain balance and organise the football before releasing.

commonErrors.error: Players slow after leaving congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate immediately into transition.

commonErrors.error: Team fails to react after a turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Change roles and attack the opposite direction at once.

progressions: Allow match-like legal tackling.
Remove the marked zones and gates.
Add scoreboard and time-pressure conditions.
Increase defensive numbers in the final zones.
Introduce position-specific starting roles.
Continue the possession into a full forward-entry scenario.
Compare assessment results across multiple training blocks.
regressions: Use bump pads instead of players.
Allow players to reset between zones.
successIndicators: Move away from pressure with the first step.
Transfer and protect the football correctly.
Maintain safe movement technique across repeated efforts.
matchApplication: The assessment combines the movement demands of contested possession, side pressure, body contact, multiple defenders and supporting teammates. It determines whether players can transfer evasion and movement technique into realistic Australian football pressure while retaining possession and progressing the football.

title: Overlap-to-Underlap Live Choice
primarySkill: Selecting an overlap or underlap from live defensive information
objective: Develop the ability of a support runner to select an outside overlap or inside underlap according to the defender’s positioning.
groundSize: Channels approximately 25 metres long and 16 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback.
setup:
Position one ball carrier at the starting gate.
Place one support runner three metres behind the football.
Position one defender six metres ahead of the ball carrier.
Mark an outside overlap gate and an inside underlap gate.
Position a second defender beyond the gates.
Place a finishing target at the end of the channel.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier and support runner enter the channel.
The first defender advances and protects either the inside or outside lane.
The support runner scans the defender and delays the movement.
If the defender closes inside, the support runner accelerates outside on an overlap.
If the defender closes outside, the support runner cuts underneath on an underlap.
The ball carrier engages the defender and releases into the selected running lane.
The receiver attacks the second defender.
The original ball carrier continues into the opposite support lane.
The attackers use a handball exchange or evasion to pass the second defender.
The possession finishes with a disposal to the target.
Rotate attackers and defenders after each repetition.
coachingPoints: The support runner must begin behind the football.
Delay the decision until the defender’s position is clear.
Select the lane the defender has surrendered.
Do not announce the movement too early.
Maintain safe crossing distance on an underlap.
The ball carrier must engage pressure before releasing.
Lead the receiver into forward space.
The original ball carrier must continue supporting.
Re-establish separate lanes after the first exchange.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the support runner scans the defender.
Whether the selected movement matches the available lane.
Whether overlap and underlap timing is delayed appropriately.
Whether the ball carrier engages pressure.
Whether safe spacing is maintained.
Whether both attackers remain involved after the first disposal.

commonErrors.error: Runner chooses a movement before seeing the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Hold behind and wait for the defensive commitment.

commonErrors.error: Underlap crosses directly across the ball carrier’s feet.
commonErrors.correction: Enter diagonally with safe separation.

commonErrors.error: Overlap runner begins too early and becomes stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Delay the acceleration until the defender closes inside.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier releases without engaging pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Carry forward until the defender commits.

commonErrors.error: Original ball carrier stops after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Fill the opposite support lane immediately.

progressions: Remove the marked gates.
Allow controlled tackling.
Add a recovering defender from behind.
Permit the runner to use a switchback when both lanes close.
Continue into a three-versus-two transition.
Require a running kick to finish.
successIndicators: Begin support from behind the football.
Select the correct overlap or underlap.
Continue possession beyond the second defender.
matchApplication: Support runners cannot rely on a predetermined overlap. Defenders may protect either the corridor or outside lane, requiring the runner to recognise space and adjust between an overlap, underlap or delayed movement.

title: Stoppage Win Spread Pattern
primarySkill: Spreading into support after a stoppage win
objective: Develop an immediate team spread that gives the first possession winner several exit and continuation options after a stoppage.
groundSize: A central stoppage circle approximately 12 metres in diameter connected to three 20-metre exit lanes.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback.
setup:
Create a central stoppage area.
Position two teams around the stoppage.
Mark an inside, outside and rear exit lane.
Position one target beyond each lane.
Nominate inside, outside and balance players for the initial repetitions.
Use controlled stoppage contact.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach initiates a ball-up or boundary-style stoppage.
Both teams contest for possession.
When a team wins the football, its outside players accelerate away from the congestion.
One player presents inside, one moves outside and one remains behind the football.
The possession winner scans and selects an exit.
If unable to carry, the player releases to one of the support options.
After the first disposal, the team continues spreading into three lanes.
The team scores by connecting with a target within eight seconds.
If possession changes, the new attacking team spreads immediately.
The team losing possession applies pressure and protects the corridor.
Reset with varied stoppage starting positions.
coachingPoints: Spread must begin as possession is being won, not afterwards.
Outside players should move away from congestion.
Maintain one rear balance option.
The first possession winner must protect the football before forcing a disposal.
Inside and outside runners must use separate lanes.
Lead support players with the handball.
Continue movement after the first exit.
The team losing possession must close central space immediately.
Communicate the first available outlet.
Avoid all support players running forward at the same depth.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether support movement begins before possession is fully secured.
Whether the team establishes width and depth.
Whether one rear option remains available.
Whether the possession winner chooses an appropriate exit.
Whether the first disposal leads the receiver.
Whether defensive transition begins immediately after a loss.

commonErrors.error: Players remain watching the stoppage after possession is won.
commonErrors.correction: Begin spreading as soon as the football moves towards a teammate.

commonErrors.error: Every support player runs forward.
commonErrors.correction: Assign and retain one rear balance player.

commonErrors.error: Outside runners remain too close to congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate into wider lanes.

commonErrors.error: First possession winner disposes without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the football and identify the clearest outlet.

commonErrors.error: Losing team reacts slowly.
commonErrors.correction: Nearest player pressures while others close central exits.

progressions: Remove nominated support roles.
Allow full legal stoppage contact.
Add a second possession phase after the first target.
Vary the stoppage location.
Add scoreboard and time pressure.
Continue into an inside-50 entry.
regressions: Begin with a coach handballing to a nominated possession winner.
Use passive opponents outside the stoppage.
successIndicators: Establish inside, outside and rear options.
Continue running after the first disposal.
Connect with a target at speed.
matchApplication: Winning the stoppage is only valuable when the team can escape the immediate congestion. Rapid spread creates outlets for the possession winner and supports continued movement into open play.

title: Wing-to-Corridor Switch Run
primarySkill: Switching movement from the wing into the corridor
objective: Develop coordinated movement that draws pressure towards the wing before using a delayed runner to switch possession into the corridor.
groundSize: An area approximately 50 metres long and 40 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback.
setup:
Mark a wing lane, central corridor and far-side lane.
Position one ball carrier in the wing lane.
Place a defender between the wing and corridor.
Position one delayed inside runner behind the football.
Place one far-side runner holding width.
Position a forward target beyond the corridor.
Use controlled defensive pressure.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier begins moving along the wing.
The defender shifts towards the boundary-side possession.
The inside runner initially holds behind the football.
The far-side runner maintains width and moves forward gradually.
When the defender commits towards the wing, the inside runner accelerates diagonally into the corridor.
The ball carrier releases by handball or short kick to the inside runner.
The inside receiver enters the corridor facing forward.
The receiver selects the central forward target or the far-side runner.
The original ball carrier continues along the wing as support.
Defenders recover after the first disposal.
The attacking group scores by reaching a target in controlled possession.
Rotate roles and repeat from both wings.
coachingPoints: The inside runner must delay until pressure commits towards the wing.
Maintain far-side width throughout the early phase.
The wing ball carrier should scan inside before receiving where possible.
Use a diagonal forward release rather than a flat transfer.
The inside receiver should enter facing attack.
Preserve the far-side option to stretch recovering defenders.
The original ball carrier must continue moving.
Avoid forcing the corridor when the defender has not shifted.
Recycle or continue down the wing if the inside lane remains closed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the inside runner delays correctly.
Whether the defender is drawn towards the wing.
Whether far-side width is preserved.
Whether the release travels forward into the corridor.
Whether the receiver scans both finishing options.
Whether movement continues after the switch.

commonErrors.error: Inside runner enters the corridor before pressure commits.
commonErrors.correction: Hold behind and delay the acceleration.

commonErrors.error: Far-side runner narrows towards the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain width to stretch the defensive structure.

commonErrors.error: Wing ball carrier turns blindly inside.
commonErrors.correction: Scan and release rather than carrying directly into pressure.

commonErrors.error: Transfer is flat or behind the runner.
commonErrors.correction: Deliver diagonally into the forward path.

commonErrors.error: Original ball carrier stops after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Continue along the wing as a return option.

progressions: Add a second corridor defender.
Remove marked lanes.
Allow the attacking team to continue down the wing when appropriate.
Add a recovering defender from the far side.
Finish with an inside-50 entry.
Begin from a defensive turnover.
regressions: Begin the inside runner closer to the receiving lane.
successIndicators: Draw defensive pressure towards the wing.
Enter the corridor with forward momentum.
Keep the original ball carrier involved.
matchApplication: Teams often use the wing to move opposition defenders before attacking through the corridor. A delayed inside runner can exploit the central space created when the defence overcommits towards boundary-side possession.

title: Forward-Half Repeat Movement
primarySkill: Repeating forward movement after the first option is denied
objective: Develop coordinated forward movement that creates a second and third receiving option when the initial lead is ignored or closed.
groundSize: Forward 50 or an area approximately 45 × 45 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback.
setup:
Position one ball carrier outside forward 50.
Place three or four forwards inside the area.
Position an equal or slightly smaller number of defenders.
Mark several starting zones but leave leading lanes open.
Place one front-and-square support player near the top of the scoring area.
Use controlled marking and body pressure.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier approaches forward 50.
One forward makes the initial lead.
Defenders close or deny the first lead.
The unused forwards hold their lanes rather than following the first movement.
The first forward continues through the lead and clears space.
A second forward attacks the newly available lane.
If the second option is also closed, another forward rotates or doubles back into a third space.
The front-and-square player adjusts beneath the likely contest.
The ball carrier delivers to the best available option.
After a mark, forwards immediately provide play-on support.
After a spill, players react to win the ground football.
Defenders counterattack if they win possession.
Rotate forward and defensive roles after several entries.
coachingPoints: The first lead must clear space if it is not used.
Avoid several forwards leading into the same lane.
Secondary movement should begin after the defence reacts.
Use changes of pace to create separation.
Maintain one player front and square.
The ball carrier must remain patient enough to see repeat movement.
Unused forwards must keep moving into useful positions.
Reorganise quickly after a mark or spill.
Maintain forward pressure following a turnover.
Communicate who is creating space and who is attacking it.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the first lead creates space when unused.
Whether secondary movement is delayed appropriately.
Whether forwards occupy separate lanes and depths.
Whether front-and-square support adjusts with the football.
Whether the ball carrier recognises later options.
Whether players react immediately after a mark, spill or turnover.

commonErrors.error: All forwards follow the initial lead.
commonErrors.correction: Hold separate starting lanes until the first movement clears space.

commonErrors.error: First forward stops after being ignored.
commonErrors.correction: Continue through and remove the defender from the next lane.

commonErrors.error: Secondary lead begins too early.
commonErrors.correction: Wait for the defence to commit to the first movement.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier delivers automatically to the first option.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the developing second and third movements.

commonErrors.error: Front-and-square player stands beneath the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Hold several metres in front and adjust to the football’s flight.

progressions: Remove starting zones.
Add full legal marking pressure.
Introduce a recovering midfielder.
Add scoreboard and time scenarios.
Continue into a defensive transition after turnover.
Allow forwards to communicate and assign live movement roles.
regressions: Predetermine the first and second leads.
Use handball feeds before kicking entries.
successIndicators: Time secondary and third leads correctly.
React immediately to the possession outcome.
matchApplication: Forward entries often fail when every player makes one lead and then stops. Repeat movement forces defenders to continually adjust and creates new scoring lanes when the first option is unavailable.

title: Full-Ground Evasion and Transition Game
primarySkill: Applying movement principles across full-ground transition
objective: Develop the ability to apply individual evasion and coordinated team movement continuously across defensive exit, midfield transition and forward entry.
groundSize: Full oval or approximately two-thirds of an oval for reduced numbers.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback.
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Use normal field positions where numbers allow.
Mark optional reference gates through defensive exit, wings and corridor.
Award normal scores plus movement bonus points.
Establish legal match-like contact.
Position spare footballs at both ends.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins with a defensive possession or turnover.
The team in possession must create wide, central and rear support.
Individual ball carriers may use evasion when a genuine running lane exists.
After every disposal, the player must continue into a new support position.
Teams may attack through the corridor, wing or switch according to pressure.
Forwards coordinate space creation, repeat leads and front-and-square movement.
Bonus points are awarded for:
Escaping pressure with a controlled evasion.
Completing an overlap or underlap.
Switching to the weak side.
Using a rear release to escape a press.
Scoring after coordinated forward movement.
Defenders score bonus points for forcing a predictable boundary exit or winning a turnover through movement pressure.
After every turnover, teams transition immediately.
Play continues in four-to-six-minute blocks.
Coaches provide brief feedback between blocks.
Remove reference gates as execution improves.
coachingPoints: Maintain movement structure without becoming rigid.
Scan before receiving.
Use individual evasion only when it improves the team’s position.
Continue moving after disposal.
Preserve width, depth and rear support.
Rotate lanes when teammates move through the same area.
Recognise when to switch, recycle or attack directly.
Coordinate forward movements.
React immediately to turnovers.
Maintain movement quality under fatigue.
Communicate field position, pressure and available space.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether individual evasion connects with team movement.
Whether the team maintains width and depth through transition.
Whether players move after disposing.
Whether lane rotations prevent crowding.
Whether forward movement is coordinated.
Whether defensive recovery begins immediately.
Whether movement quality remains effective under fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Players use evasion when a simple disposal is available.
commonErrors.correction: Select the action that best advances team possession.

commonErrors.error: Team movement collapses towards the football.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish wide, central and rear lanes.

commonErrors.error: Disposers stop after releasing.
commonErrors.correction: Continue into the next support or balance position.

commonErrors.error: Players force forward movement against a set defence.
commonErrors.correction: Use rear support or switch the football.

commonErrors.error: Forwards lead into the same space.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger movements and use different lanes.

commonErrors.error: Teams fail to react after a turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Nearest players change roles immediately.

progressions: Remove all marked reference gates.
Add score-and-time scenarios.
Play with unequal numbers for selected blocks.
Increase the consequence of turnovers.
Apply position-specific movement targets.
Extend work periods to match quarter demands.
regressions: Use controlled tackling or two-hand touch.
Pause after turnovers for brief organisation.
Limit each team to selected movement patterns.
Reduce the length of playing blocks.
successIndicators: Apply evasion without disconnecting from teammates.
matchApplication: This game integrates the full chapter into continuous Australian football. Players must combine balance, acceleration, evasion, football protection, support movement and team structure across realistic full-ground phases.
relatedDrills: EA-060 – Pressure, Contest and Evasion Phase Assessment

title: Evasion, Agility and Movement Chapter Final Assessment
primarySkill: Complete evasion, agility and movement assessment
objective: Assess each player’s ability to apply the complete range of individual and team movement skills developed throughout EA-001 to EA-079.
groundSize: Full oval or approximately two-thirds of an oval, plus a separate technical assessment area.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback.
setup:
Create four assessment phases:
Individual Movement Phase
Athletic stance, balance, acceleration, deceleration and change of direction.
Evasion and Pressure Phase
Ball carrying, sidestep, football protection, contact balance and pressure escape.
Support and Team Movement Phase
Overlap, underlap, lane rotation, staggered support, rear release and weak-side movement.
Match Application Phase
Full-ground transition game with live turnovers, defensive exit and forward entry.
Divide players into balanced assessment groups.
Assign coaches to specific assessment categories.
Use ratings of Developing, Competent, Advanced or Elite.
Complete familiarisation repetitions before formal scoring.
Set contact appropriate to the age and competition level.
Prepare individual assessment sheets covering technique, decision making, movement intensity and match transfer.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players begin in the individual movement phase.
Each player completes:
A reaction start.
A controlled deceleration.
A left and right change of direction.
A single-leg balance and recovery action.
Players progress to the evasion and pressure phase.
Each player collects a football, responds to a defender, protects possession and exits through an available gate.
Players complete one repetition with trailing pressure, one with frontal pressure and one with controlled side contact.
Groups then enter the support and team movement phase.
Players complete live overlap-or-underlap choices, rear releases, lane exchanges and weak-side switches against defenders.
Coaches assess movement timing, spacing, scanning and disposal execution.
The session finishes with the match application phase.
Teams play a full-ground or reduced-ground transition game.
Bonus points reward effective movement behaviours from the chapter.
Turnovers remain live and teams must transition immediately.
Coaches record individual and team outcomes across all phases.
Each player receives one demonstrated strength and one priority development area.
The assessment concludes when every player has completed all phases and at least two match-application blocks.

whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Athletic stance and movement readiness.
Balance on both sides.
First-step acceleration.
Controlled deceleration.
Safe change-of-direction mechanics.
Ability to evade different pressure angles.
Football protection through movement and contact.
Decision to evade, release or recycle.
Movement after disposal.
Width, depth and lane discipline.
Timing of support runs.
Rear and weak-side movement.
Forward movement coordination.
Immediate turnover reaction.
Technical consistency under fatigue.
Transfer of isolated skills into match play.

commonErrors.error: Player prioritises speed over balance.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce pace and rebuild the movement from a controlled position.

commonErrors.error: Significant difference exists between left and right sides.
commonErrors.correction: Add targeted repetitions on the less-developed side.

commonErrors.error: Player uses a predetermined evasion.
commonErrors.correction: Require the defender or available space to be identified first.

commonErrors.error: Football becomes exposed during contact.
commonErrors.correction: Transfer earlier and protect with legal body position.

commonErrors.error: Player stops after disposing.
commonErrors.correction: Continue into the next support, overlap or balance role.

commonErrors.error: Team movement crowds the football.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish width, depth and separate lanes.

commonErrors.error: Rear support disappears during attack.
commonErrors.correction: Assign one player to remain behind the football.

commonErrors.error: Forwards make simultaneous leads into one area.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger movements and use different angles.

commonErrors.error: Players react slowly after turnovers.
commonErrors.correction: Change roles immediately and communicate possession status.

commonErrors.error: Technique deteriorates excessively under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Increase recovery or reduce the intensity until quality returns.

Use two-hand touch instead of tackling.
Assess without a football before adding possession.
successIndicators: Choose appropriate evasion or release options.
Maintain width, depth and rear support.
Time overlaps, underlaps and lane rotations.
Maintain technical and tactical movement quality under fatigue.
Transfer individual skills into realistic team play.
matchApplication: The final assessment evaluates whether the chapter’s movement skills have transferred from isolated technique into realistic Australian football. It covers the complete progression from athletic stance and body control through individual evasion, pressure escape, coordinated support, transition and full-ground match application.
